BEHIND THE EXPERIMENT

Real questions.
An experimental model.

This version is a working interface and a transparent neural simulation. It does not contain the MaleCNS connectome or recreate a living fly’s preferences.

What you are watching
192 leaky integrate-and-fire units in six synthetic groups. Their actual spikes light up the network and populate the raster. Activity in the output group determines the result.
How it chooses
Visual and chemical controls inject current. Synthetic excitatory and inhibitory connections propagate it. Output spikes in the final three simulated seconds determine pursuit (above 6 spikes per output neuron per second), pass (below 3), or no clear response. These thresholds and inputs are design assumptions, not measured fly biology.
What stays honest
The wiring and trial seed are fixed. The same settings reproduce the same result. Bios and photographs do not enter the model. “Pass” means low model output, not demonstrated rejection. Node positions are a diagram, not brain anatomy. The six-second simulation plays more slowly for readability.
The scientific next step
Replace synthetic wiring with a documented MaleCNS circuit, justify sensory encoding and readouts, then compare predictions with published experiments and perturbation controls. Simulating more neurons alone does not validate behaviour.
